To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Departures from the Buyer playbook and recommended pushback
**Status:** Privileged. Buyer internal only.

---

## 1. Headline points

1. **The Seller has opened at two of our authority-gated fallbacks.** These are the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and the 18-month claims period. Neither fallback is available to us. Amelia Frost has given no written authority for either, for any draft. We should counter at our starting positions (25% / AUD 6m and 24 months). We should not treat the Seller's figures as a convenient landing point.
2. **The draft removes our fraud carve-out.** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature". This takes in fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. This point is non-negotiable and no one on our side can waive it.
3. **A general override would collapse the separate regimes.** The proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" would pull Title, Capacity, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants into the general cap, basket and time limits. Together with the explicit proposal to put title and capacity under the general regime, this is the most important drafting risk in the package.
4. **The Disclosure Letter helps us on the facts.** It candidly confirms open gaps on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses and DD-006. Its general disclosure (§1.1–1.2) and the Buyer-knowledge bar in cl 8.3 would then stop us claiming on exactly those gaps. We should use the specific admissions and strike the general disclosure.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability architecture

| # | Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment and pushback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m. 20% only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. | **Reject.** No authority exists. Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not signal that 20% is available. If the team wants to move, it must first obtain written authority from Amelia Frost referencing this draft. |
| A2 | De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** This is 5x our position. At AUD 25k, many realistic individual warranty breaches in a business this size could never be claimed. |
| A3 | Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, tipping basket (first dollar) | **Reject on both size and mechanism.** An excess-only basket is a permanent deductible: the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of every breach in aggregate. Insist on AUD 50k tipping. |
| A4 | General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months | **Reject.** 18 months is a gated fallback with no approval. A 24-month period covers at least two full audit and financial-year cycles post-Completion. |
| A5 | Universal application of limitations (cl 12.3/13) | "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate. No hidden general-regime override. | **Delete.** This reverses the default so that every carve-out must be drafted perfectly or it fails. The default should be the opposite: general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims. Each other category should carry its own expressly stated regime. |
| A6 | Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject firmly.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. Capping them at 20% would leave us recovering at most AUD 4.8m if title failed. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept that. |
| A7 | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Not waivable. | **Non-negotiable.** Insert an express overriding clause: nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller or its officers, employees, agents or advisers. Under NSW law, contractual exclusions of fraud are in any event likely to be read restrictively or be unenforceable. The ACL s 18 misleading-conduct risk around non-reliance also arises. We should still not rely on the general law and should draft the carve-out expressly. |
| A8 | Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | OPEN. No assumed resolution and no assumed unlimited liability. | **Do not accept as settled.** Reply that the tax and IP positions remain open and are not agreed. Do not concede that they fall under the general regime. We should also not overstate our own position; we have not agreed unlimited liability either. Reserve them for separate negotiation. |

### B. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge

**B1. General disclosure (Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2; Schedule 7).** The letter discloses the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- *Departure:* The playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and deemed disclosure.
- *Why it matters:* Without this change, every gap the letter itself flags would be "disclosed" and could not be claimed. That includes Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses, DD-006 and the renewals.
- *Pushback:* Delete §1.1 and §1.2. A disclosure qualifies a warranty only where it is made **against a specific warranty** with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Data room documents count only where they are specifically referenced, with the relevant extract identified. Disclosure must never qualify Title, Capacity, Tax or the specific indemnities.

**B2. §1.4 (no admission).** This is broadly market and can largely stay. It must not be read as limiting the Seller's specific indemnities or covenants. Add "without prejudice to the indemnities and covenants".

**B3. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer "or its advisers" knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- *Departure:* The playbook requires deletion of blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusions.
- *Why it matters:* This is broader than general disclosure. It imputes adviser knowledge and constructive "discoverability". Combined with §1.1, the warranties would be close to worthless.
- *Pushback:* Delete cl 8.3. If a qualifier must exist, it should go the other way: Seller knowledge qualifiers limited to named Seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry. Any qualifier must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### C. Conditions and completion mechanics

**C1. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3).**
- *Facts:* DD-002 shows Bluefen at about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. Change-control consent is required under cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. Disclosure §2 confirms that no final consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions has been provided.
- *Seller position:* Reasonable endeavours only, and the condition is satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
- *Problem:* Delivery of a letter is not the same as an **effective** consent. If the cl 11.3 conditions are unmet, the consent may not be operative and the change-control right could survive Completion. Reasonable endeavours is also too weak for a customer worth about 30% of revenue.
- *Pushback:* Make effective, unconditional Bluefen consent, with evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, a condition precedent that only the Buyer can waive. The Seller should give a stronger endeavours obligation, all reasonable or best endeavours. Add a long-stop date and a Buyer termination right.

**C2. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7).**
- *Facts:* About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2. Disclosure §3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included.
- *Seller position:* A release "to be provided following Completion".
- *Problem:* Change of control may trigger default under cl 8.1. On a debt-free basis, we would be paying full price while security remains over the target.
- *Pushback:* Require (i) a current payout letter, (ii) direct repayment from Completion funds into the funds flow, and (iii) executed security releases and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.

**C3. Employee bonuses (funds flow; DD-005).**
- *Facts:* Conditional Completion bonuses total AUD 420,000. The Seller states they are "a matter for the Seller" but they do not appear in the funds flow. Disclosure §5 says nothing about payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- *Problem:* If the target company is the paying entity, the cost falls on us after Completion unless it is captured. That is a silent price leak of at least AUD 420k plus any on-costs.
- *Pushback:* Either include the bonuses as a specific funds-flow or Debt line item, with triggered on-costs and paid through payroll at Completion, or make them expressly Seller-funded and backed by a specific indemnity. Confirm whether payroll tax, super and other on-costs are triggered rather than assuming either way.

### D. Specific risk items

**D1. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010).** The Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment.
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. As the disclosure notes, this is not independent verification of non-payment. Equally, we have no evidence that it has been paid. No receipt and no confirmatory assignment exist.
- *Pushback:* Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have valid rights in the Ironquay deliverables, including third-party claims. Preserve the SOW3 cure: pay out any amount properly due at or before Completion and obtain a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable. Verify the AUD 180k status through Ironquay and bank records. Do not assume it is owed or that it has been paid.

**D2. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DD-006).**
- The Seller calls this "preliminary operational, not expected to be material". The disclosure itself says that access, scope and notification obligations are **not established**. The export involves about 1,240 records.
- *Our framing:* We should not call it a confirmed breach, assert a notification duty, or put a number on it. We should also not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation.
- *Pushback:* Add a pre-Completion covenant requiring the Seller to preserve logs and evidence, continue a proper investigation, provide regular written updates, and give the Buyer access to the findings. Include a notifiable data breach assessment under the Privacy Act if that becomes relevant. Add a specific indemnity for any loss arising from the incident, so it sits outside the general basket and disclosure.

**D3. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011; AUD 330,000).** The Seller says these are ordinary-course costs. The disclosure says it does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- *Pushback:* Treat this as a diligence question, not a concession either way. Request the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, and whether amounts are prepaid or accrued at the Locked Box or Completion Accounts date. Do not automatically claim Debt treatment or a price deduction until the facts support it. Reserve the right to treat amounts as Debt or a working-capital adjustment if they are found to be pre-Completion liabilities.

**D4. Title (DD-012).** The Seller relies solely on its own share register.
- *Pushback:* DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller and is not independent proof. Require independent evidence: an ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Seller and the shares, share certificates, constitution and shareholder agreement review for pre-emption or transfer restrictions, Seller board approvals and authority, and confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or encumbrances. Back this with Title warranties under the separate 100% / 6+ year regime (see A6).

**D5. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The disclosure frames these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not consent triggers on a share sale. This is plausible but is the Seller's characterisation. Have our team confirm by reviewing the actual clauses for any change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording. Make lease notification a Completion deliverable.

---

## 3. Process note

The covering letter describes the package as "fair and balanced". That is advocacy, not a reason to move. On nearly every limitation point the Seller has opened at or beyond our worst authorised position, and in several places beyond anything we have authorised. Our mark-up should respond from our starting positions. Any concession on the cap or the claims period requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. The fraud carve-out is not available as a concession at all.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable**
1. Restore the full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).
2. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" override. General limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims.
3. Keep Title and Capacity in a separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.

**Counter at playbook (no fallback authority exists)**
4. Cap at 25% / AUD 6m, not 20% / AUD 4.8m.
5. Claims period of 24 months, not 18.
6. De minimis of AUD 5k and a tipping basket of AUD 50k, not AUD 25k and an AUD 250k excess-only basket.

**Disclosure and knowledge**
7. Strike general disclosure (§1.1–1.2) and require specific fair disclosure against specific warranties.
8. Delete the Buyer-knowledge bar in cl 8.3. Any qualifier should cover only named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry, and should never apply to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.

**Completion mechanics**
9. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Buyer-only CP, with stronger endeavours, a long-stop date and a termination right.
10. Riverlark: a payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, and releases and PPSR discharges at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
11. Bonuses: include the AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs as a funds-flow line item, or make them Seller-funded with an indemnity.

**Specific risks**
12. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, obtain a confirmatory assignment, and verify the AUD 180k independently.
13. DD-006: add preservation, investigation and update covenants plus a specific indemnity. Make no assumption of breach, harm, notification duty or quantum.
14. Sandbar: run diligence on the AUD 330k before taking any position. No automatic Debt or price treatment.
15. Title: obtain independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence beyond the DD-012 register.
16. Tax/IP: state that these remain open and are not settled under the general regime.
17. Lease and Mossvale: verify the Seller's "no consent" characterisation against the actual clauses.

I can turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up or a short issues list for the Seller's counsel if helpful.

- *Seller position:* Reasonable endeavours only, and the condition is satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
- *Problem:* Delivery of a letter is not the same as an **effective** consent. If the cl 11.3 conditions are unmet, the consent may not be operative and the change-control right could survive Completion. Reasonable endeavours is also too weak for a customer worth about 30% of revenue.
- *Pushback:* Make effective, unconditional Bluefen consent, with evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, a condition precedent that only the Buyer can waive. The Seller should give a stronger endeavours obligation, all reasonable or best endeavours. Add a long-stop date and a Buyer termination right.

**C2. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7).**
- *Facts:* About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2. Disclosure §3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included.
- *Seller position:* A release "to be provided following Completion".
- *Problem:* Change of control may trigger default under cl 8.1. On a debt-free basis, we would be paying full price while security remains over the target.
- *Pushback:* Require (i) a current payout letter, (ii) direct repayment from Completion funds into the funds flow, and (iii) executed security releases and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.

**C3. Employee bonuses (funds flow; DD-005).**
- *Facts:* Conditional Completion bonuses total AUD 420,000. The Seller states they are "a matter for the Seller" but they do not appear in the funds flow. Disclosure §5 says nothing about payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- *Problem:* If the target company is the paying entity, the cost falls on us after Completion unless it is captured. That is a silent price leak of at least AUD 420k plus any on-costs.
- *Pushback:* Either include the bonuses as a specific funds-flow or Debt line item, with triggered on-costs and paid through payroll at Completion, or make them expressly Seller-funded and backed by a specific indemnity. Confirm whether payroll tax, super and other on-costs are triggered rather than assuming either way.

### D. Specific risk items

**D1. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010).** The Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment.
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. As the disclosure notes, this is not independent verification of non-payment. Equally, we have no evidence that it has been paid. No receipt and no confirmatory assignment exist.
- *Pushback:* Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have valid rights in the Ironquay deliverables, including third-party claims. Preserve the SOW3 cure: pay out any amount properly due at or before Completion and obtain a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable. Verify the AUD 180k status through Ironquay and bank records. Do not assume it is owed or that it has been paid.

**D2. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DD-006).**
- The Seller calls this "preliminary operational, not expected to be material". The disclosure itself says that access, scope and notification obligations are **not established**. The export involves about 1,240 records.
- *Our framing:* We should not call it a confirmed breach, assert a notification duty, or put a number on it. We should also not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation.
- *Pushback:* Add a pre-Completion covenant requiring the Seller to preserve logs and evidence, continue a proper investigation, provide regular written updates, and give the Buyer access to the findings. Include a notifiable data breach assessment under the Privacy Act if that becomes relevant. Add a specific indemnity for any loss arising from the incident, so it sits outside the general basket and disclosure.

**D3. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011; AUD 330,000).** The Seller says these are ordinary-course costs. The disclosure says it does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- *Pushback:* Treat this as a diligence question, not a concession either way. Request the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, and whether amounts are prepaid or accrued at the Locked Box or Completion Accounts date. Do not automatically claim Debt treatment or a price deduction until the facts support it. Reserve the right to treat amounts as Debt or a working-capital adjustment if they are found to be pre-Completion liabilities.

**D4. Title (DD-012).** The Seller relies solely on its own share register.
- *Pushback:* DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller and is not independent proof. Require independent evidence: an ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Seller and the shares, share certificates, constitution and shareholder agreement review for pre-emption or transfer restrictions, Seller board approvals and authority, and confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or encumbrances. Back this with Title warranties under the separate 100% / 6+ year regime (see A6).

**D5. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The disclosure frames these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not consent triggers on a share sale. This is plausible but is the Seller's characterisation. Have our team confirm by reviewing the actual clauses for any change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording. Make lease notification a Completion deliverable.

**Non-negotiable**
